relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: He continued his studies under his great-grandfather's guidance and at Mysore University.

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: While at university, he studied logic and Sanskrit, working with Brahmashri Shivakumar Shastry, "one of the greatest grammarians of the age".

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: He stated that he learned the Mimamsa from Brahmasri Trilinga Rama Shastri.

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: In 1914, he once again left for Banaras to attend classes at Queen's College

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: Krishnamacharya eventually left Queen's College to study the ႐aႅdarŕana (six darshanas) in Vedic philosophy at Patna University, in Bihar

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: He received a scholarship to study Ayurveda under Vaidya Krishnakumar of Bengal.

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: He further claimed that he studied with the yoga master Sri Babu Bhagavan Das

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: Krishnamacharya claimed in his Yoga Makaranda that at the suggestion of Gaᑅgānāth Jhā, he sought to further his yoga studies by seeking a master named Yogeshwara Ramamohana Brahmachari

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: In 1931, Krishnamacharya was invited to teach at the Sanskrit College in Mysore.

relations.subject: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
relations.evidence: In Madras, Krishnamacharya accepted a job as a lecturer at Vivekananda College.

relations.subject: Indra Devi
relations.evidence: Krishnamacharya's students included many of yoga's most renowned and influential teachers: Indra Devi (1899–2002)

relations.subject: K. Pattabhi Jois
relations.evidence: Krishnamacharya's students included many of yoga's most renowned and influential teachers: Indra Devi (1899–2002); K. Pattabhi Jois (1915–2009)

relations.subject: B. K. S. Iyengar
relations.evidence: Iyengar, his brother-in-law and founder of Iyengar Yoga, credits Krishnamacharya with encouraging him to learn yoga as a boy in 1934.

relations.subject: T. K. V. Desikachar
